problem: The line 'external stakeholders regulate or depend on it' is loose: passengers and clerks also depend on the system, yet they are primary stakeholders. A student may think any dependent party is external.
fix: Say: primary stakeholders use or benefit from the system; secondary stakeholders build or support it (developers, maintainers, support staff, trainers); external stakeholders sit outside the organisation (regulators, government agencies, external payment networks). Note that external stakeholders may also depend on the system.

problem: 'Secondary stakeholders support it' is too narrow and can be read as only operational support. Standard usage also covers people involved in developing and maintaining the system.
fix: Write: secondary stakeholders are involved in building or supporting the system, such as developers, testers, maintainers, trainers and support staff.

problem: The text says 'convenience features become later options', but the very next sentence delivers one-click in the same release as a remembered profile after authentication. The two sentences read as contradictory.
fix: Say: mandatory rules are fixed first; convenience features are then negotiated. Here the audit trail is mandatory, and one-click is reduced to a remembered passenger profile after authentication rather than full anonymous one-click.

problem: The answer makes OTP mandatory, but Section 3 only declares the audit trail mandatory; OTP is not labelled mandatory anywhere. A student comparing text and answer sees a mismatch.
fix: Either add OTP to the mandatory list in Section 3 ('audit trail and OTP are mandatory; one-click becomes a remembered profile after authentication'), or reword the Q4 answer to match the text.

problem: Splitting the 20-minute conflict-resolution block equally across the five stakeholder groups suggests each group resolves conflicts separately, which conflicts with the chapter's own advice to resolve by joint ranking, not by giving each side its own slot.
fix: Reframe part (c) as time per group for preparing or presenting their conflict list, or ask for the average time per participant (20 ÷ 12 ≈ 1.67 minutes) instead of per group.

problem: The accessibility representative is treated as an important stakeholder in the text and invited to the workshop, but does not appear in the stakeholder map figure, so the figure and text do not match.
fix: Either add an accessibility representative node to the figure on the high-interest side, or state in the caption that the figure shows only the main groups and that the accessibility representative is added separately.
